newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Wave of deals rack up rich premiums.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Wave of deals rack up rich premiums.

text.p: In one of the strongest days for small to mid-sized initial public offerings in recent memory, six companies went public on Tuesday, with four winning substantial premiums.
Analysts said there were enough powerful deals still in the pipeline to keep the market strong in the short-term future.
"So long as the tape remains healthy, the IPO market will remain as it has been," said Vincent Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald.
The companies that went public today:
-- Cal Dive International Inc shares jumped more than 31 percent, surging 4-3/4 to 19-3/4.
The 3.6 million shares sold for $15 each, the top of their IPO pricing range of $14 to $15. That range was revised higher from an earlier range of $12 to $14. The deal raised roughly $54 million.

This was the second try at going public for Houston-based Cal Dive, which provides services such as deep-sea building, inspection, maintenance, repair and salvage to the offshore natural gas and oil industry in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico.

Cal Dive withdrew an earlier IPO proposal that came before its April announcement that it would sell a 32 percent equity stake to an affiliate of Paris-based Coflexip SA for $35 million. The two companies have a joint venture for projects in deep-water oil and gas fields in the Gulf of Mexico.
-- New York Stock Exchange debutante Pierce Leahy Corp jumped 28 percent, one of the best performing stocks on the Big Board for the morning session.
The stock rose five to 23 from its price of $18, which was at the top of price talk of $15 to $18.

Smith Barney was the lead underwriter of the deal, which raised about $95.4 million in total. Smith Barney also bought a large block of 1,141,200 shares earlier at 22-1/2. That accounted for about half of the shares traded this morning, with volume at roughly 2.2 million at midday.
Pierce Leahy, based in King of Prussia, Pa., manages archived records, including microfilm, and video tapes. The bulk of its profits, 95 percent, come from storing paper.

Pierce Leahy has also filed for a high-yield offering of $100 million in senior subordinated notes due in 2007. In early June, Moody's said the company's "high debt and lease burden may continue to strain fixed-charge coverages and the ability of the company to tap a large amount of bank debt poses acquisition risk. The planned public offering of equity will provide the company with a much needed alternative financing source for growth".
-- Schick Technologies Inc added 2-3/8 20-7/8 from an IPO price of $18.50, near the top of a range of $17 to $19 and above the first range of $15 to $17.
Schick makes digital radiography devices used in dental X-rayt computer imaging systems. It is based in New York's Long Island City area.

-- Hanover Compressor Co, the largest IPO on Tuesday, rose 2-1/4 to 21-3/4. The natural gas compression services company sold 4,166,667 shares for $19.50 each, raising about $81.25 million. Selling shareholders also offered stock in the 6.6 million-share IPO.
-- Heska Corp, which makes animal health products, eked out a gain of 3/8 to 8-7/8, but only after lead underwriter Credit Suisse First Boston sharply scaled back terms of the deal.
-- Schuff Steel shares rose 1/4 to 8-1/4 from an IPO price of $8 each, below a range of $9 to $11.
-- Another IPO, SpectRx Inc, went public later in the day. Shares were flat at their IPO price of $7. Lead underwriter Hambrecht & Quist also cut back terms of the deal ahead of the pricing.
The company is involved in developing products that offer painless and bloodless alternatives to monitor glucose levels and screen for diabetes and infant jaundice.
((Jennifer Westhoven, Wall Street Desk 212 859 1881))
